summary: The article proposes that Robinhood halted GME trading on January 28, 2021 (day 35 of the threshold-security list) because Citadel's failures to deliver shifted liability to Robinhood under Reg SHO § 242.203(b2). The author theorizes that Citadel intentionally structured its short position to make others responsible for delivery, and that the "MOASS" is delayed while regulators negotiate how to squeeze Citadel specifically without creating systemic collapse. The piece uses correct descriptions of market mechanics and real dates but presents an unsupported causal chain as explanation for the January halt.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Robinhood halted trading on day 35 because they became liable to deliver shares Citadel failed to deliver, triggering Reg SHO § 242.203(b2) obligations
key_claims.note: The regulatory framework and Jan 28 timing vs. 35-day threshold are documented (pages 12, 19-20), but the causal mechanism—that Citadel failures specifically triggered Robinhood's liability—was never confirmed by regulators. SEC report attributed the January halt to capital/collateral constraints.

key_claims.claim: Claims that the MOASS is delayed because Citadel took hostages and regulators are negotiating to ensure Citadel is squeezed before smaller entities
key_claims.note: No MOASS occurred by mid-2026. Short interest fell from ~122% to ~20% by Feb 2021 and remained low. No evidence of persistent 100%-1000%+ hidden short interest emerged.

key_claims.claim: Claims that multiple brokers halted trading at their own T+35 thresholds independently, not by Citadel orchestration
key_claims.note: Multiple brokers did halt; the timing overlap with threshold dates is plausible (page 27-28), but this is post-hoc rationalization, not documented evidence of the mechanism.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Robinhood cost basis errors after transfers were caused by this T+35 settlement failure mechanism
key_claims.note: Cost basis errors were real and reported (page 21-24), but cause remains unconfirmed; could be system errors, T+35 mechanics, or other factors.

key_claims.claim: Claims that Citadel, as a market maker, has regulatory privileges and exemptions that make it resilient to squeezes
key_claims.note: Accurate description of market maker privileges; confirmed by hindsight (page 31-32).

key_claims.claim: Claims that failures to deliver went on for 35+ days and obligated brokers to deliver before Citadel
key_claims.note: Reg SHO T+35 rules are real (pages 12-13). FTDs and naked shorting are documented phenomena. But the specific Citadel→Robinhood FTD chain was never substantiated by any regulator.

key_claims.claim: Claims that those responsible for the situation will receive only minimal punishment due to cooperation with regulators
key_claims.note: By mid-2026, Citadel has not been margin-called or collapsed; no major criminal charges have emerged. Light enforcement relative to the alleged severity is consistent with the prediction (pages 41-44).

validity_rationale: The article correctly describes Reg SHO settlement mechanics and the Jan 28 threshold-list timing, but chains these into an unsupported causal theory linking Citadel failures to Robinhood's halt. The core prediction—that a MOASS is pending—was falsified by 2026. No regulator confirmed the Citadel→Robinhood FTD mechanism; the SEC report attributed the run-up mainly to retail sentiment and positive buying pressure, not to failure-to-deliver cascades. The author explicitly frames this as a 'tinfoil hat' conspiracy theory, and while market mechanics are accurately described, the inference from real data to a sweeping systemic hostage scenario is unsupported.
